gloss: loyal kindness, steadfast love; faithful, devoted one; (also) shame, reproach
summary: חֶסֶד is kindness that keeps faith: what one party does for another out of a bond already made, a covenant, an oath, a kinship or a kindness received, and so it goes again and again with אֱמֶת “truth, faithfulness” and with בְּרִית “covenant”. Between men it is the kindness Abraham asks of Sarah, Rahab of the spies, David of Jonathan and shows to Jonathan's son; from Yahweh it is the steadfast love he swore to Abraham and to David, “keeping the covenant and the חֶסֶד”, “abounding in חֶסֶד and truth”, and “his חֶסֶד is forever”; from man to God it is loyal devotion, which Yahweh desires “and not sacrifice” (Hos 6:6, quoted by Jesus). The adjective חָסִיד is the one who keeps such faith: Yahweh's faithful ones, who made a covenant with him by sacrifice (Psa 50:5), his “faithful one” who will not see the pit (Psa 16:10, of Christ's resurrection in Acts 2 and 13), and Yahweh himself. The same spelling also means “shame, reproach” (Lev 20:17; Pro 14:34; the piel Pro 25:10), the only sense the root has in the Peshitta's Syriac; the stork חֲסִידָה is the root's bird.

words.gloss: loyal kindness, steadfast love, faithfulness; devotion; (rarely) shame, reproach
words.summary: About 250 times, over half in the Psalms. It is always done, shown, kept or remembered within a relationship, and it is the ground of a further request (“as I have done חֶסֶד with you, do with me”, Gen 21:23; Jos 2:12). Its plural חֲסָדִים is the acts of such kindness, Yahweh's or a man's (Gen 32:11; Isa 55:3; Neh 13:14; 2Ch 32:32). In two verses the same spelling is “shame, a disgrace”, the sense the root has in Aramaic and Syriac; the two meanings are kept together here as one spelling.

senses.definition: The kindness one person does another to whom he is bound, by covenant, oath, kinship, hospitality or a kindness received: keeping faith in deed, often for the sake of the dead or for those who cannot repay.

evidence.note: Abimelech asks Abraham to swear: “according to the חֶסֶד that I have done with you, you shall do with me and with the land where you have sojourned.”
David to Jonathan: “Do חֶסֶד with your servant, for you have brought your servant into a covenant of Yahweh with you.”
“Show me the חֶסֶד of Yahweh, that I die not; and do not cut off your חֶסֶד from my house for ever.”
“Is there still anyone left of the house of Saul, that I may do him חֶסֶד for Jonathan's sake?”
“That I may do him the חֶסֶד of God.”
Rahab: “Swear to me by Yahweh, since I have done חֶסֶד with you, that you also will do חֶסֶד with my father's house, and give me a true sign.”
“When Yahweh gives us the land, we will deal with you חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת.”
Jacob to Joseph, hand under the thigh: “Deal with me חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת: do not bury me in Egypt.”
Abraham to Sarah: “This is your חֶסֶד that you shall do to me: everywhere we go, say of me, He is my brother.”
“If you will deal חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת with my master, tell me.”
Joseph to the cupbearer: “Remember me … and do חֶסֶד with me.”
“Show us the way into the city, and we will do חֶסֶד with you.”
Israel “did not do חֶסֶד with the house of Jerubbaal-Gideon, according to all the good he had done Israel”.
The Kenites spared, “for you did חֶסֶד with all the sons of Israel when they came up from Egypt”.
To the men of Jabesh-gilead who buried Saul: “Blessed be you of Yahweh, that you have done this חֶסֶד with your lord.”
“I will do חֶסֶד with Hanun son of Nahash, as his father did חֶסֶד with me.”
Absalom to Hushai: “Is this your חֶסֶד with your friend?”
“Do חֶסֶד to the sons of Barzillai … for so they came near to me when I fled.”
“The kings of the house of Israel are kings of חֶסֶד”: kings who keep faith with those who submit.
“Yahweh do חֶסֶד with you, as you have done with the dead and with me.”
“Your last חֶסֶד is better than the first, in that you did not go after young men”: Ruth's loyalty to the family of her dead husband.
“A man of חֶסֶד does good to his own soul, but the cruel (אַכְזָרִי) troubles his own flesh.”
“What is desired in a man is his חֶסֶד, and a poor man is better than a liar.”
“Many a man proclaims his own חֶסֶד, but a faithful man (אִישׁ אֱמוּנִים) who can find?”
“To him who is fainting, חֶסֶד from his friend.”
“Execute true judgment, and do חֶסֶד וְרַחֲמִים each man with his brother.”
Esther “won חֶסֶד before him”: favour shown her. Also Est 2:17, with חֵן.

senses.definition: Yahweh's kindness to his people, kept because of his covenant and oath to the fathers and to David: shown in deliverance, guidance, forgiveness and the preserving of life, and lasting for ever.

evidence.note: Yahweh's own proclamation of his name: “merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת, keeping חֶסֶד for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin.”
“The faithful God, who keeps the covenant and the חֶסֶד with those who love him and keep his commandments, to a thousand generations.”
“Yahweh your God will keep for you the covenant and the חֶסֶד which he swore to your fathers.”
“Doing חֶסֶד to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.” Also Deu 5:10.
“In your חֶסֶד you led the people you redeemed.”
“Blessed be Yahweh, the God of my master Abraham, who has not forsaken his חֶסֶד and his truth toward my master.”
Jacob: “I am too small for all the חֲסָדִים and all the truth that you have shown your servant.”
“Yahweh was with Joseph and extended חֶסֶד to him”, and gave him favour with the keeper of the prison.
Moses: “Pardon the iniquity of this people according to the greatness of your חֶסֶד, as you have forgiven this people from Egypt until now.”
Of David's seed: “I will chasten him … but my חֶסֶד shall not depart from him, as I took it from Saul.”
“I will make with you an everlasting covenant, חַסְדֵי דָוִד הַנֶּאֱמָנִים”: the sure acts of kindness promised to David; quoted Act 13:34 of the resurrection.
“For ever I will keep my חֶסֶד for him, and my covenant shall stand fast with him.”
“My חֶסֶד I will not break off from him, nor be false to my faithfulness.”
“Where are your former חֲסָדִים, Lord, which you swore to David in your faithfulness?”
“You will give truth to Jacob, חֶסֶד to Abraham, which you swore to our fathers from days of old.”
“The mountains may depart … but my חֶסֶד shall not depart from you, nor shall my covenant of peace be removed.”
“In a little wrath I hid my face … but with everlasting חֶסֶד I will have compassion on you.”
“Give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good, for his חֶסֶד is for ever”: the refrain of all 26 verses, through creation, the exodus and the gift of the land.
“And gave their land for an inheritance, for his חֶסֶד is for ever; an inheritance to Israel his servant.”
“The חֲסָדִים of Yahweh, that we are not consumed, for his compassions do not fail.”
“The חֶסֶד of Yahweh is from everlasting to everlasting on those who fear him.”
“Who redeems your life from the pit, who crowns you with חֶסֶד וְרַחֲמִים.”
“Be gracious to me, God, according to your חֶסֶד; according to the abundance of your compassions blot out my transgressions.”
“Surely goodness and חֶסֶד shall follow me all the days of my life.”
“All the paths of Yahweh are חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת to those who keep his covenant and his testimonies.”
“Yahweh, your חֶסֶד is in the heavens, your faithfulness to the clouds.”
“Yahweh delights in those who fear him, those who hope in his חֶסֶד.”
“I am Yahweh, doing חֶסֶד, justice and righteousness in the earth, for in these I delight.”
“I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have drawn you with חֶסֶד.”
“I will betroth you to me in righteousness and in justice, and in חֶסֶד and in compassion.”
Jonah quotes Exo 34:6: “a gracious God and merciful, slow to anger and abounding in חֶסֶד.” Also Jol 2:13; Neh 9:17; Psa 103:8; 145:8.
“He does not keep his anger for ever, because he delights in חֶסֶד.”
“Our God has not forsaken us in our bondage, but has extended חֶסֶד to us before the kings of Persia.”
“The great and awesome God, who keeps the covenant and חֶסֶד with those who love him.” Also 1Ki 8:23; Dan 9:4.
“Blessed be he of Yahweh, who has not forsaken his חֶסֶד to the living and to the dead.”
“I will sing of the חֲסָדִים of Yahweh for ever.”

senses.definition: A man's or a people's loyal love toward Yahweh, shown in keeping faith with him and with his people; in the plural, the faithful deeds a man has done.

evidence.note: “For I desire חֶסֶד and not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings”; quoted by Jesus, Mat 9:13; 12:7.
“I remember the חֶסֶד of your youth, the love of your betrothal, when you went after me in the wilderness, in a land not sown.”
“Your חֶסֶד is like a morning cloud, like the dew that goes early away.”
“There is no truth, and no חֶסֶד, and no knowledge of God in the land”: then swearing, lying, murder, theft, adultery (Hos 4:2).
“What does Yahweh require of you but to do justice, and to love חֶסֶד, and to walk humbly with your God?”
“Sow for yourselves in righteousness, reap according to חֶסֶד.”
“Keep חֶסֶד and justice, and wait on your God continually.”
“Those who regard empty vanities forsake their חֶסֶד”: the loyalty they owe.
“Let not חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת forsake you; bind them on your neck.”
“By חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת iniquity is atoned, and by the fear of Yahweh men depart from evil.”
“He who pursues righteousness and חֶסֶד finds life.”
“The law of חֶסֶד is on her tongue.”
“Men of חֶסֶד are taken away, none considering that the righteous is taken away from the evil.”
“All flesh is grass, and all its חֶסֶד like the flower of the field”: man's goodliness and loyalty fade, “but the word of our God stands for ever” (Isa 40:8); quoted 1Pe 1:24.
“Remember me, my God … and do not wipe out my חֲסָדִים that I have done for the house of my God and its services.”
“The rest of the acts of Hezekiah and his חֲסָדִים.” Also of Josiah, 2Ch 35:26.

senses.definition: A disgrace: a deed that brings reproach on those who do it, as incest does on a man and sin on a people.

evidence.note: A man who takes his sister and sees her nakedness: “חֶסֶד הוּא, it is a disgrace, and they shall be cut off in the sight of the sons of their people.”
“Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a חֶסֶד to peoples”: set against “exalts”, a disgrace.

evidence.locator: Gen.24.12; Jer.2.2; Hos.6.6; Psa.103.17, חֶסֶד → ἔλεος; Mic.6.8; 7.20 → ἔλεον; ἔλεος renders חֶסֶד ×142, with πολυέλεος ×9 for רַב־חֶסֶד (Exo.34.6)

evidence.note: “Go and learn what this means: I desire mercy (ἔλεος) and not sacrifice”: Hos 6:6. Again Mat 12:7.
“His mercy is to generations of generations on those who fear him”: Psa 103:17.
“To remember mercy, as he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed for ever”: Mic 7:20.
“To perform mercy with our fathers and to remember his holy covenant, the oath which he swore to Abraham our father.”
“Justice and mercy and faithfulness”: the weightier matters of the law, as Mic 6:8.

greek.gloss: holy, devout; (neuter plural) holy things, sure mercies

evidence.note: “That he raised him from the dead, no more to return to corruption, he has spoken thus: I will give you τὰ ὅσια Δαυὶδ τὰ πιστά”: Isa 55:3, חַסְדֵי דָוִד הַנֶּאֱמָנִים.
“All flesh is as grass, and all the glory of man as the flower of grass … but the word of the Lord abides for ever”: Isa 40:6–8.
Elizabeth: “to take away my reproach (ὄνειδος) among men”; the Peshitta has חֶסְדִּי, the Syriac word of this root.

parallels.note: “Truth, faithfulness”: חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת, kindness that is true to its word, of men and of Yahweh.
“Faithfulness”: in the heavens, to all generations, sworn to David.
“Covenant”: “who keeps the covenant and the חֶסֶד”; “my חֶסֶד … and my covenant of peace”.
“Righteousness”: done with חֶסֶד, pursued with it.

opposites.note: “Cruel”: the man of חֶסֶד against the cruel man.
Pursuing the poor: “he did not remember to do חֶסֶד, but pursued the poor and needy man”.

phrases.gloss: do kindness with, keep faith with
for his steadfast love is for ever
who keeps the covenant and the steadfast love

words.gloss: faithful, devoted, godly; (as noun) faithful one
words.summary: 32 times, all but five in the Psalms. Mostly a noun with “his” or “your”: Yahweh's faithful ones, those bound to him by covenant, set beside his servants and those who fear him. Twice Yahweh calls himself or is called חָסִיד (Jer 3:12; Psa 145:17).

senses.gloss: faithful one, godly one (of Yahweh's people)
senses.definition: One who keeps faith with Yahweh, bound to him by his covenant: his servants, those who fear him, whom he guards, keeps, and does not abandon to the grave.

evidence.note: “Gather to me my חֲסִידִים, those who made a covenant with me by sacrifice.”
“Know that Yahweh has set apart the חָסִיד for himself.”
“Save, Yahweh, for the חָסִיד has ceased, for the faithful (אֱמוּנִים) have vanished from the sons of man.”
“The חָסִיד has perished from the earth, and there is none upright among men; they all lie in wait for blood.”
“The bodies of your servants … the flesh of your חֲסִידִים to the beasts of the earth.”
“You will not abandon my soul to the grave (שְׁאוֹל); you will not give your חָסִיד to see the pit”: applied to the resurrection of Jesus in Act 2:27–31 and 13:35–37.
“Yahweh loves justice and does not forsake his חֲסִידִים; they are kept for ever.”
“He guards the feet of his חֲסִידִים, but the wicked are silenced in darkness.”
“Guarding the paths of justice and keeping the way of his חֲסִידִים.”
“You who love Yahweh, hate evil; he guards the souls of his חֲסִידִים.”
“Precious in the eyes of Yahweh is the death of his חֲסִידִים.”
“Love Yahweh, all his חֲסִידִים; Yahweh preserves the faithful (אֱמוּנִים).”
“Guard my soul, for I am חָסִיד; save your servant who trusts in you.”
“He will speak peace to his people and to his חֲסִידִים.”
“You spoke in vision to your חָסִיד”: of the covenant with David.
Of Levi: “your Thummim and your Urim are with your חָסִיד, whom you tested at Massah.”
“Let your priests be clothed with righteousness, and your חֲסִידִים shout for joy.” Again Psa 132:16; 2Ch 6:41.
“Let the חֲסִידִים exult in glory … to execute on the nations the judgment written; this honour is for all his חֲסִידִים.”
“Praise for all his חֲסִידִים, the sons of Israel, a people near to him.”
“For this let every חָסִיד pray to you.”
“Plead my cause against a nation not חָסִיד; from the deceitful and unjust man deliver me.”

senses.definition: Of Yahweh himself: faithful in his dealings, keeping his kindness and not his anger.

evidence.note: “Return, faithless Israel … for I am חָסִיד, says Yahweh; I will not keep anger for ever.”
“Yahweh is righteous in all his ways and חָסִיד in all his works.”

evidence.locator: Psa.16.10, חֲסִידְךָ → ὅσιόν; Psa.50.5; 145.17 → ὅσιος; 2Sa.22.26; Psa.18.26 → ὁσίου; ὅσιος renders חָסִיד ×17 in all its forms

evidence.note: Peter quotes Psa 16:10, “you will not give your ὅσιον to see corruption”, and says David died and was buried, and spoke of the resurrection of the Christ (Act 2:29–31).
Paul sets Psa 16:10 beside Isa 55:3 (Act 13:34): David saw corruption, “but he whom God raised saw no corruption” (Act 13:36–37).
“Such a high priest became us, ὅσιος, harmless, undefiled.”
“For you alone are ὅσιος”: of God, as Psa 145:17.

words.summary: Six times: an unclean bird, large-winged, nesting in the trees and keeping the seasons of its migration. In form it is the feminine of חָסִיד, “the faithful (bird)”, but no verse explains the name, and no cognate is known; the only hint in scripture is Job 39:13–16, where the ostrich's wing is set beside the stork's and the ostrich is hard toward her young. Its link to the root is not shown.

senses.definition: A large unclean bird with broad wings, which nests in trees and keeps its appointed times of passage.

evidence.note: Among the birds not to be eaten: “and the חֲסִידָה, the heron after its kind.” Also Deu 14:18.
“Even the חֲסִידָה in the heavens knows her appointed times … but my people do not know the judgment of Yahweh”: a bird of passage.
“Where the birds make their nests; the חֲסִידָה, the fir trees are her house.”
Two women with “wings like the wings of the חֲסִידָה”, lifting the ephah between earth and heaven.
“The wing of the ostriches beats joyfully; is it the pinion of the חֲסִידָה, and plumage?” The ostrich leaves her eggs in the dust and “is hard toward her young” (Job 39:14–16).

words.gloss: show oneself faithful; put to shame
words.summary: Three uses in two stems, one for each side of the spelling: the hithpael “show oneself חָסִיד” in the twin verses 2Sa 22:26 and Psa 18:26, and the piel “put to shame” in Pro 25:10. So little use fixes neither firmly; each rests on its sibling nouns.

senses.definition: Of Yahweh: to deal as one who keeps faith, toward the one who keeps faith with him.

evidence.note: “With the חָסִיד you show yourself faithful (תִּתְחַסָּד), with the blameless man you show yourself blameless.”
The same words in David's song.

senses.definition: To bring disgrace on someone by making his fault known.

evidence.note: “Debate your case with your neighbour, and do not reveal another's secret, lest he who hears יְחַסֶּדְךָ, and your evil report not turn away” (Pro 25:9–10).

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܚܣܕ (ḥassed), always of reproach: where the Greek has ὀνειδίζω. The Peshitta has no “kindness” of this root; for mercy it uses ܪܚܡ.

senses.definition: To heap shame on someone in words: to revile the righteous, or to rebuke the unrepentant and unbelieving.

evidence.note: “Blessed are you when they reproach you (דַּמְחַסְּדִין) and persecute you and say every evil word against you falsely for my sake.”
“When they separate you and reproach you and cast out your name as evil.”
“The robbers who were crucified with him reviled him.” Also Mrk 15:32.
“Then he began to upbraid the cities in which most of his mighty works were done, because they did not repent.”
He “upbraided their unbelief and hardness of heart”.
God “gives to all freely and does not reproach”: giving without shaming the one who asks.

senses.definition: To suffer reproach, for the hope of the gospel or the name of Christ.

evidence.note: “If you are reproached for the name of Christ, blessed are you.”
“For this we labour and are reproached, because we hope in the living God.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܚܣܕܐ (ḥesdā), for ὀνειδισμός and ὄνειδος: the reproach borne for Christ.

senses.definition: Disgrace in the eyes of others: of barrenness, of a fault, and above all the reproach of Christ, borne by those who follow him.

evidence.note: Moses “esteemed the reproach of Christ (חֶסְדֵּהּ דִּמְשִׁיחָא) greater riches than the treasures of Egypt.”
“Let us go out to him outside the camp, bearing his reproach.”
“Christ did not please himself, but as it is written, The reproaches of those who reproach you fell on me”: Psa 69:10, where the Hebrew has חֶרְפָּה.
Elizabeth: “to take away my reproach among men”: the shame of barrenness.
“You endured a great conflict of sufferings, with reproach and afflictions” (Heb 10:32–33 in the Greek numbering).
An overseer must have a good report from outsiders, “lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the adversary”.
“The reproaches of your revilers (דַּמְחַסְּדָנַיךְ) fell on me”: Psa 69:10.

cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Targums: the Hebrew's kindness, at Gen 39:21 and the plural at Gen 32:11 and Psa 107:43. Mostly in Targums of verses with חֶסֶד, so it may echo the Hebrew rather than show independent Aramaic use.

evidence.locator: s.v. חֶסֶד ² (חִסְדָּא), citing Targ. Gen. XXXIX, 21; Targ. O. Gen. XXXII, 11 (pl. חִסְדַּיָּא); Targ. Ps. CVII, 43

cognates.note: A Syriac “mercy” beside the commoner “reproach” of the same spelling. The Peshitta New Testament never uses it, and its use elsewhere is not yet followed to texts; it may be borrowed from the Hebrew or Jewish Aramaic.

evidence.note: “mercy, kindness; favour, forbearance, clemency”; compares Hebrew חֶסֶד.

cognates.note: Neo-Punic, on a statue: “the Pious (ḥsd); righteous were his deeds” (KAI 145 II 7). The same noun as Hebrew חָסִיד, and set beside righteousness of deeds as the Psalms set it.

evidence.note: “n.m. PIOUS PERSON. KAI 145 II 7 (NPu) … the Pious; righteous were his deeds.”

evidence.locator: SEM001362 ḥsd [kind] V, PUN000715 ḥsd [pious] N

cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic, in the Targum of Psa 18:26 and 145:10 for חָסִיד, and in the Talmud of pious and conscientious men.

evidence.locator: s.v. חֲסִיד (ch.), citing Targ. Ps. XVIII, 26; Targ. Ps. CXLV, 10 (pl. חֲסִידַיָּא); B. Kam. 30a

cognates.gloss: be put to shame; (pael, aphel) jeer at, disgrace; (ithpaal) be reviled
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic: the reproach side of the spelling, the same as the Peshitta's. The Targum of Pro 25:10 keeps the root for the Hebrew piel (נַחְסְדָךְ), and the Targum of 1Sa 17:36 uses it of Goliath's defiance of the armies of the living God.

evidence.locator: s.v. חֲסַד (ch.), citing Targ. Ps. XXXIV, 6; XL, 15; Pa. Af. Targ. I Sam. XVII, 36; Targ. Prov. XXV, 10; Ithpa. Targ. Ps. LXXI, 24

cognates.gloss: envy; wish another deprived of a blessing
cognates.note: Arabic envy, the wish that another lose a good thing he has: ill will toward another's standing, which reproach expresses. The sound match is exact (ḥ, s, d), but envy is not shame, so the link to the reproach sense is uncertain. Arabic shows ḥ behind ח.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 567, art. حسد, حَسَدَهُ (n7959)
evidence.note: “He envied him for the thing … i.e. he disliked that he should possess it, and wished that it might depart from him.”

doctrine.statement: Yahweh's חֶסֶד is bound to his oath: he “keeps for you the covenant and the חֶסֶד which he swore to your fathers” (Deu 7:9, 12), and the prophet ends, “you will give truth to Jacob, חֶסֶד to Abraham, which you swore to our fathers from days of old” (Mic 7:20). What was sworn to Abraham was the land: “all the land which you see, to you I will give it, and to your seed for ever” (Gen 13:15). Yet Abraham was given “no inheritance in it, not even a foot's breadth; yet he promised to give it to him for a possession, and to his seed after him” (Act 7:5), and the fathers “died in faith, not having received the promises” (Heb 11:13, 39–40). When the Christ was about to be born, Zechariah and Mary both took up Mic 7:20: God has come “to perform mercy with our fathers and to remember his holy covenant, the oath which he swore to Abraham our father” (Luk 1:72–73), “as he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed for ever” (Luk 1:54–55). From the verses: the חֶסֶד promised to Abraham is a sworn kindness not yet performed to him, and it is performed through Jesus, his seed, in the inheritance of the land.

Yahweh promised David a son whose throne he would establish for ever: “my חֶסֶד shall not depart from him” (2Sa 7:12–16); “for ever I will keep my חֶסֶד for him … his seed I will make to endure for ever, and his throne as the days of heaven” (Psa 89:29–30), sworn and not to be broken (Psa 89:34–38). Isaiah calls it “an everlasting covenant, the sure חֲסָדִים of David” (Isa 55:3), and David sang, “you will not abandon my soul to the grave, you will not give your חָסִיד to see the pit” (Psa 16:10). Peter says David “both died and was buried, and his tomb is with us to this day”, and that he “did not ascend into the heavens”; being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn to set one of his seed on his throne, “he foresaw and spoke of the resurrection of the Christ” (Act 2:27–34). Paul joins the two verses: God raised Jesus “no more to return to corruption”, and so gave “the sure mercies of David”; David “fell asleep and was laid with his fathers and saw corruption, but he whom God raised saw no corruption” (Act 13:34–37). The angel told Mary that God would give her son “the throne of his father David” (Luk 1:32–33). From the verses: the חֶסֶד sworn to David is kept in the resurrection of Jesus to an endless life, to sit on David's throne; David himself is dead and in the grave, awaiting it.

Yahweh says, “I desire חֶסֶד and not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings” (Hos 6:6), when Israel's חֶסֶד was “like a morning cloud” (Hos 6:4) and there was “no truth, no חֶסֶד, no knowledge of God in the land” (Hos 4:1). Micah asks whether Yahweh wants thousands of rams, and answers, “to do justice, and to love חֶסֶד, and to walk humbly with your God” (Mic 6:6–8). Jesus twice sent his critics to Hos 6:6: “go and learn what this means”, when he ate with sinners, and when his disciples were blamed on the sabbath (Mat 9:13; 12:7); and he named “justice and mercy and faithfulness” the weightier matters of the law (Mat 23:23). From the verses: the offerings were never a substitute for keeping faith; what Yahweh asks of his people is the same loyal kindness he shows them, toward him and toward one another (Zec 7:9).

note: BDB files the noun and the verb twice, “goodness, kindness” (h.ed.ab, h.ed.aa) and “shame, reproach” (h.ee.ab, h.ee.aa), with the same tokens; the words here name the h.ed keys only. The noun's 249 tokens include the names at 1Ki 4:10 (בֶּן־חֶסֶד) and 1Ch 3:20 (יוּשַׁב חֶסֶד), which have their own name entries (hesed, jushab-hesed). Kindness and shame are kept in one entry as one spelling; whether they are one older root (as ברך bless/curse is sometimes argued) or two is open. No cognate shows which older sound stands behind ח for the kindness side: Aramaic, Syriac and Punic do not keep ḥ and ḫ apart, and no Arabic or Ugaritic cognate of the kindness sense was found. Arabic حَشَدَ “gather to help” (Lane, art. حشد) and Sabaean ḥsd (Biella p. 192, doubtful) would answer to Hebrew חשׂד, not חסד, and are not recorded. The brief's New Testament quotation Mat 5:11 ← Psa 23:6 is an artefact: the Peshitta's ḥsd “reproach” aligned to Hebrew חֶסֶד “kindness”. The Syriac ܚܣܕܐ “mercy” (Wiktionary) is not yet followed to a Syriac text or to Payne Smith. The Peshitta verse Heb 10:32 is 10:33 in the Greek. Psalm references are in the Hebrew numbering.
